pattern.summary: 9 questions, attempt any 5, each carries 20 marks. All theory. The last 2–3 questions are usually short notes, 'distinguish between' or 'comment on' with internal choice.

sessionNotes.2023-06: The printed sub-marks add to 10 per question, but the paper is 100 marks with 5 equal questions, so each is counted as 20.

choosing: The paper is entirely theory. Planning, organisation structure, leadership, motivation and marketing (PLC, pricing) return almost every session.
Questions with internal choice ('any two of the following') are good picks — you choose the notes you know.

topics.name: Planning
topics.summary: Meaning, nature, importance, principles, process; plans vs policies; long vs short range.
points: Planning: deciding in advance what to do, how, when and by whom — the first function of management.
Nature: goal-oriented, primary function, pervasive (all levels), continuous, futuristic, involves choice, mental exercise.
Importance: gives direction, reduces uncertainty, avoids overlapping and waste, promotes innovation, basis for control, helps decision-making.
Principles: contribution to objectives, primacy, pervasiveness, efficiency, flexibility, commitment, navigational change, limiting factor.
Process: set objectives → develop premises → identify alternatives → evaluate → select the best → implement → follow up.
Types of plans: objectives, strategies, policies, procedures, methods, rules, programmes, budgets.
Plans vs policies: a plan is a course of action for a goal; a policy is a general guide to thinking and decisions (e.g. 'promote from within').
topics.frame: Definition (quote Koontz: 'deciding in advance what to do, how to do it, when to do it and who is to do it') → headed points → a flow diagram of the process → conclusion.
mistakes: Listing process steps without one line of explanation each.

topics.name: Organisation Structure
topics.summary: Types of structure (line, functional, line & staff), formal vs informal, departmentation, span of control, charts and manuals.
points: Organisation structure: the framework of roles, authority and relationships in an enterprise.
Line organisation: authority flows top to bottom in a straight line; simple, quick decisions, but overloads top managers.
Functional organisation (F.W. Taylor): specialists in charge of functions; expertise, but multiple bosses and confusion.
Line and staff: line managers command, staff specialists advise; suits large firms such as banks.
Formal organisation: deliberately designed roles and rules. Informal: social relations that arise naturally — managers can use it for quick communication and feedback.
Departmentation bases: function, product, territory, customer, process, time.
Span of control: number of subordinates a manager directly supervises; depends on the nature of work, ability of manager and subordinates, communication, planning.
Unity of command: each subordinate reports to one superior. Organisation chart: diagram of positions and relations. Manual: written record of policies, procedures and duties.
topics.frame: Meaning → draw a small chart of the structure → features → merits and demerits in two lists → suitability.
mistakes: Not drawing a chart — a simple diagram earns marks.

topics.name: Marketing (Concepts, PLC, Pricing)
topics.summary: Marketing concepts, marketing mix, product life cycle and pricing — asked in almost every paper.
points: Marketing: identifying and satisfying customer needs profitably.
Marketing concepts: production, product, selling, marketing, societal marketing.
Marketing mix (4 Ps): product, price, place, promotion.
Product life cycle: introduction (low sales, high cost), growth (sales rise, competitors enter), maturity (sales peak, price competition), decline (sales fall, withdraw or revive).
Pricing approaches: cost-oriented (cost-plus, mark-up, break-even), demand-oriented (perceived value, price discrimination), competition-oriented (going-rate, sealed bid).
Sales vs marketing: sales focuses on the product and seller's needs; marketing on the customer's needs and long-term satisfaction.
topics.frame: Definition → a PLC curve diagram (sales vs time) → each stage with features and strategy → conclusion.

topics.name: Leadership & Morale
topics.summary: Meaning, styles, qualities of a leader, manager as leader, and morale.
points: Leadership: influencing people to work willingly towards group goals.
Styles: autocratic, democratic/participative, laissez-faire; also paternalistic, transactional, transformational.
Qualities: vision, integrity, communication, decision-making, empathy, confidence, initiative.
Functions: set goals, motivate, guide, represent the group, build morale, resolve conflict.
Morale: the attitude and spirit of employees towards work; influenced by pay, leadership, work conditions, recognition, job security.
Leader vs manager: a leader influences, a manager directs through authority; a good manager must also lead.
topics.frame: Definition → styles with one example each (table: style / features / suitable when) → conclusion.

topics.name: Motivation & Incentives
topics.summary: Meaning, process, Maslow and Herzberg theories, financial vs non-financial incentives.
points: Motivation: the process that stimulates people to act towards desired goals.
Process: unsatisfied need → tension → drive → search behaviour → satisfied need → reduced tension.
Maslow's hierarchy: physiological → safety → social → esteem → self-actualisation; a satisfied need no longer motivates.
Herzberg's two-factor theory: hygiene factors (pay, policy, working conditions) prevent dissatisfaction; motivators (achievement, recognition, work itself, growth) motivate.
Financial incentives: pay, bonus, profit sharing, commission. Non-financial: status, recognition, job enrichment, security, participation, career growth.
Bonus vs incentive: a bonus is a lump-sum extra payment; incentives are linked to performance.
topics.frame: Definition → theory with a pyramid diagram (Maslow) or two-column table (Herzberg) → criticism → conclusion.
mistakes: Drawing Maslow's pyramid in the wrong order.

topics.name: Innovation, Skill Development & Start-ups
topics.summary: Innovation types and process, skill development initiatives, Start-up India, Make in India, MSMEs.
points: Creativity: generating new ideas. Invention: creating something new. Innovation: turning an idea into a useful product, service or process.
Types of innovation: product, process, marketing, organisational; incremental vs radical.
Innovation process: idea generation → screening → concept development → business analysis → development/prototype → testing → commercialisation.
Skill development in India: Skill India Mission, PMKVY, National Skill Development Corporation, apprenticeships, ITIs.
Start-up India: funding support, tax benefits, easier compliance, incubators. Incubator: supports start-ups with space, mentoring and funds.
Make in India: encourages manufacturing in India. 'Made in India' is the label on goods produced here.
MSME: micro, small and medium enterprises — classified by investment and turnover.
topics.frame: Meaning → steps in a flow chart → Indian examples (schemes, companies) → conclusion.

topics.name: CSR & Business Ethics
topics.summary: Corporate social responsibility, its paradigm shift and theories, and components of business ethics.
points: CSR: a company's responsibility towards society and stakeholders beyond profit.
Paradigm shift: from charity/philanthropy → stakeholder responsibility → CSR as strategy and sustainability; mandatory CSR spending under the Companies Act, 2013 (section 135).
Theories: shareholder (Friedman), stakeholder, social contract, legitimacy, triple bottom line (people, planet, profit).
Benefits: goodwill, customer loyalty, employee morale, better community relations, long-term survival.
Business ethics: moral principles guiding business conduct.
Components: code of ethics, ethics committee, ethics training, whistle-blowing, top management commitment.
topics.frame: Definition → points with headings → Indian example (e.g. Tata, Infosys) → conclusion.

topics.name: E-commerce & Emerging Trends
topics.summary: E-commerce vs traditional commerce, m-commerce, Digital India, outsourcing, franchising.
points: E-commerce: buying and selling over the internet. Types: B2B, B2C, C2C, C2B.
Features: 24×7, global reach, low cost, digital payments, personalisation.
Traditional vs e-commerce: physical vs online; limited hours vs 24×7; local vs global; cash vs digital payment.
M-commerce: e-commerce on mobile devices. Digital wallet: stores money for online payments (e.g. Paytm).
Digital India: digital infrastructure, digital services on demand, digital literacy.
Outsourcing: contracting work to an outside firm. Offshoring: moving work to another country.
Franchising: franchisor lets a franchisee use its brand and system for a fee (e.g. McDonald's).
topics.frame: Definition → comparison table (traditional vs e-commerce) → merits and limitations → conclusion.

topics.name: Business, Commerce, Trade & Profession
topics.summary: Business vs profession vs employment, commerce, trade and aids to trade, industry, objectives of business.
points: Economic activities (for money) vs non-economic (for love, social or religious reasons).
Business: regular production or exchange of goods and services for profit. Profession: specialised service needing qualification (doctor, lawyer). Employment: working for others for salary.
Commerce = trade + aids to trade. Aids to trade: transport, banking, insurance, warehousing, advertising, communication.
Trade: internal (wholesale, retail) and external (import, export, entrepot).
Industry: primary (extractive, genetic), secondary (manufacturing, construction), tertiary (services).
Objectives of business: economic (profit, growth, market share), social, human, national.
topics.frame: Definition → classification chart → table comparing business, profession and employment → conclusion.

topics.name: Joint Stock Company & Public Enterprises
topics.summary: Company features and types, private vs public, OPC, government companies, Maharatna/Navratna/Miniratna.
points: Company: an artificial person created by law, with separate legal entity, perpetual succession, common seal, limited liability, transferable shares.
Types: private and public; by liability (limited by shares, by guarantee, unlimited); government company; holding and subsidiary; listed and unlisted.
Private vs public: members (min 2 / min 7), share transfer restricted vs free, cannot / can invite the public.
One Person Company (OPC): one member, a nominee required; fewer compliance requirements (no AGM, fewer board meetings).
Government company: at least 51% of paid-up capital held by the government.
Public enterprises: owned and run by the government; Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna status gives greater financial autonomy.
topics.frame: Definition → features as headed points → types in a chart → merits and limitations → conclusion.

topics.name: Decision-Making
topics.summary: Meaning, relationship with planning, and the steps of scientific decision-making.
points: Decision-making: choosing the best course of action from alternatives.
Planning and decision-making are linked: every plan involves decisions, and decisions need planning premises.
Steps: identify the problem → gather information → develop alternatives → evaluate → choose → implement → follow up.
Types: programmed vs non-programmed, strategic vs routine, individual vs group.
topics.frame: Definition → flow chart of steps → one example → conclusion.

topics.name: Co-operative Organisation
topics.summary: Meaning, features, types, merits, limitations and objectives of co-operatives.
points: Co-operative: a voluntary association of people who work together for mutual benefit (e.g. Amul).
Features: voluntary membership, democratic control (one member one vote), service motive, separate legal entity on registration, limited liability, state control.
Types: consumer, producer, marketing, credit, housing, farming co-operatives.
Merits: easy formation, limited liability, democratic, low cost. Limitations: limited capital, poor management, lack of secrecy, government interference.
Objectives: economic (cheaper goods, fair prices) and social (mutual help, equality).
topics.frame: Definition → features → types → merits and limitations table → Indian example.

topics.name: Sole Proprietorship & Partnership
topics.summary: Sole trader features, partnership deed, kinds of partners, sole vs partnership.
points: Sole proprietorship: owned and controlled by one person; unlimited liability; no separate legal entity; easy formation; full profit and control; limited capital and continuity.
Partnership: relation between persons who agree to share profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all (Indian Partnership Act, 1932).
Partnership deed contents: names, business, capital, profit-sharing ratio, interest on capital/drawings, salaries, admission, retirement, dispute settlement.
Kinds of partners: active, sleeping/dormant, nominal, partner by estoppel, minor, secret, limited.
topics.frame: Definition → features → merits and limitations → table comparing sole trader and partnership.

topics.name: Delegation of Authority
topics.summary: Meaning, principles, and why managers and subordinates avoid delegation.
points: Delegation: a manager assigns work and grants authority to a subordinate, who becomes accountable.
Elements: responsibility, authority, accountability.
Principles: delegation by results expected, parity of authority and responsibility, absoluteness of accountability, unity of command, scalar chain, exception.
Managers resist: fear of losing control, lack of trust, 'I can do it better', lack of controls.
Subordinates resist: fear of criticism, lack of information or resources, no incentive, lack of confidence.
topics.frame: Definition → the three elements → principles → barriers and how to overcome them.

topics.name: Communication
topics.summary: Process, barriers and making communication effective.
points: Communication: transfer of information and understanding from one person to another.
Process: sender → encoding → message → channel → receiver → decoding → feedback (noise can disturb any stage).
Barriers: semantic (language), psychological (attitudes, distrust), organisational (rigid rules, hierarchy), personal, physical (noise, distance).
Making it effective: clear message, right channel, two-way feedback, active listening, simple language, consistency of words and action.
topics.frame: Definition → process diagram → barriers under headings → measures → conclusion.

topics.name: Controlling
topics.summary: Meaning, nature, principles, advantages and limitations of control; control techniques.
points: Control: measuring performance against standards and correcting deviations.
Process: set standards → measure performance → compare → analyse deviations → take corrective action.
Principles: control by exception, critical point control, feedback, flexibility, suitability, economy.
Advantages: achieves goals, efficient use of resources, discipline, coordination. Limitations: costly, external factors beyond control, employee resistance.
Techniques: budgetary control, PERT/CPM, statistical quality control, management audit, break-even analysis.
topics.frame: Definition → process chart → principles → merits and limits → conclusion.

topics.name: Financial Management & Sources of Finance
topics.summary: Functions and objectives of financial management, wealth maximisation, venture capital, lease, shares.
points: Financial management: planning, raising, using and controlling funds.
Functions: investment decision, financing decision, dividend decision, working capital management.
Objectives: profit maximisation vs wealth maximisation (maximising the market value of shares) — wealth maximisation is preferred because it considers time value and risk.
Venture capital: funds for new, high-risk, high-growth ventures in exchange for equity.
Lease financing: using an asset for rent without owning it (finance vs operating lease).
Equity vs preference shares: owners with voting rights vs fixed dividend and priority in repayment.
Primary market: new securities issued. Secondary market: existing securities traded on stock exchanges.
topics.frame: Definition → functions or objectives as headed points → conclusion.

topics.name: Human Resource Management
topics.summary: Functions of HRM, challenges for HR managers, HR planning, employer–employee relations, team building.
points: HRM: acquiring, developing, motivating and retaining people.
Functions: HR planning, recruitment and selection, training and development, performance appraisal, compensation, employee relations, welfare.
Challenges: globalisation, technology, changing demographics, diversity, remote work, retention.
Employee engagement: emotional commitment of employees to the organisation.
Team building: activities that improve cooperation and trust in a group.
topics.frame: Definition → functions as headed points → conclusion.

topics.name: Choosing a Form of Organisation
topics.summary: Overview of forms and the features of an ideal form of business organisation.
points: Forms: sole proprietorship, Hindu undivided family, partnership, LLP, co-operative, joint stock company.
Ideal form features: easy formation, adequate capital, limited liability, stability, flexibility, secrecy, ease of management, minimum government regulation.
No form is ideal in all respects; the choice depends on the nature and size of business, capital needed, risk and control desired.
topics.frame: List forms → table comparing them on the features above → conclude with a reasoned choice.

topics.name: Multinational Corporations
topics.summary: Why firms become multinational; issues, trends and controversies of MNCs.
points: MNC: a company with operations in several countries, headquartered in one.
Reasons: larger markets, cheaper resources, tax benefits, avoiding trade barriers.
Benefits to host country: investment, technology, jobs, exports.
Controversies: profit repatriation, exploitation of resources and labour, transfer pricing, harming local firms, cultural impact.
topics.frame: Definition → reasons → merits and demerits → conclusion.
